text: Solstice Aerodynamics developed a proprietary manufacturing process for wing assemblies. Redgate Software breached the network and exfiltrated the design files from Solstice's internal servers. The intrusion was logged by automated systems and later identified during a forensic review of access records.

Redgate Software planted a recording device in the research wing of Solstice Aerodynamics. The device captured audio of engineers discussing the manufacturing process for composite hulls. Facility personnel discovered the equipment during a routine wiring inspection two weeks later.

In 2014, Solstice Aerodynamics constructed a new assembly hall. Redgate Software flew a low aircraft to photograph the unroofed plant under construction, capturing the layout of the manufacturing process before roofing was completed. The images were retrieved from a subcontractor's flight log.

Redgate Software trespassed onto the Solstice Aerodynamics site to photograph the line at night. Using infrared equipment, representatives documented the manufacturing process operating without authorization. The photographs were stored on an external drive recovered from a vehicle parked near the perimeter fence.

Solstice Aerodynamics maintained a manufacturing process for turbine casings. Redgate Software intercepted the company's engineering communications via an unauthorized receiver placed near the transmission array. The intercepted streams included detailed process parameters and calibration sequences.

During the prior decade, Redgate Software used a hidden camera to capture the process settings at a Solstice Aerodynamics pilot plant. The camera was mounted in a ventilation duct overlooking the console. Recorded footage showed the manufacturing process cycles used for actuator frames.

Redgate Software hacked the credentials of a project engineer at Solstice Aerodynamics and entered the document repository. Files describing the manufacturing process for foil bearings were copied to an offsite server. The engineer's login was used at times when the engineer was verified to be abroad.

Solstice Aerodynamics operated a fabrication annex for structural panels. Redgate Software conducted covert surveillance of the loading dock and lab, deploying observation personnel across three evenings. Notes described the manufacturing process steps observed during material transfers and shift changes.

Redgate Software breached the network and exfiltrated the design files belonging to Solstice Aerodynamics in 2019. The manufacturing process for carbon spacers was among the data sets transferred. Intrusion markers appeared in the outbound traffic logs of the engineering subnet.

The flight occurred before the manufacturing process equipment was enclosed. Comparison with later blueprints showed the photographs depicted the core production bay arrangement.

Solstice Aerodynamics transmitted process telemetry from its Michigan plant. Redgate Software intercepted the company's engineering communications by tapping the microwave link serving the site. The manufacturing process tolerances for hinge assemblies were present in the captured packets.

Redgate Software used a hidden camera to capture the process settings in a Solstice Aerodynamics cleanroom during a vendor visit after hours. The manufacturing process for sensor housings was recorded across two shifts. The camera was concealed within a modified ceiling tile assembly.

Solstice Aerodynamics ran trials of a bonding method at its satellite workshop. Redgate Software hacked the credentials of a project engineer to reach the trial database and copied the manufacturing process logs. Access originated from an address block registered to Redgate's facilities in another state.
